prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Mechanics, Material Structure, and Strength of Materials.

learning_outcomes.text: Introduce students to the application of engineering knowledge in studying the complexity of the physical organization of living organisms, particularly the mechanics of biological tissues and systems, comparing their behavior with typical engineering materials and structures.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Deepen knowledge in a specific area of the degree.
Broaden their perspectives and gain a critical view of the relationship with other subjects not previously taken.
Review information and communicate it effectively to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Gain practice in handling the techniques and tools typical of the course area.
Know the fundamentals of applied biomechanics.
Know the applications of biomechanics in sports, traffic accidents, and medicine, as well as the biomaterials used.
Is capable of working in a team, applying critical reasoning, making decisions, and communicating knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Anatomy and Physiology of the Locomotor System
TEMA 1: Introduction to Biomechanics: Basic Terminology and Concepts
TEMA 2: Mechanics of the Locomotor System
Levers: First, Second, and Third class
Bone behavior under various loading modes
Operating instructions. Occupational prevention and health
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts related to the subjects that make up each topic and problem-solving sessions, as well as other face-to-face group sessions such as discussion classes and common sharing.
Laboratory activities of increasing difficulty that allow students to acquire the ability to achieve autonomy in problem-solving.
Personal study, report writing, practical exercises, etc., as independent work by the student or group of students.
assessment_rules: Student's grade in ordinary examination will be: 25% laboratory practices, 60% two theoretical/practical written exams, and 15% presentation of a work. In extraordinary examination, the grade will correspond to a single written theoretical/practical exam covering the entire subject.
